antes.UserFees: Lido takes no fees from users.
antes.Fees: Staking rewards earned by all ETH staked with Lido: consensus-layer validator rewards plus execution-layer rewards (priority fees and MEV), as booked by each daily oracle report.
antes.Revenue: Lido takes a 10% fee on staking rewards; Revenue is only the DAO-treasury portion of that fee (net of the node-operator share, which is a cost of production booked as SupplySideRevenue). From Lido V2 (first report 2023-05-16) the treasury/operator split is the validator-share-weighted aggregate read from the StakingRouter at the oracle report's block; before V2 the split was a fixed 5%/5%, so half the fee is treasury.

antes.SupplySideRevenue: Staking rewards earned by stETH holders plus the node-operator share of the 10% fee (paid to operators for running validators).
antes.HoldersRevenue: Tracks LIDO bought back by the DAO as part of the LDO Accumulation Program

antes.Fees: The desk's fee on the gross premium of each weekly call the vault sells (20% at launch), fixed at the sale and recognized one hour later when the Safe can no longer void the sale; a voided sale charges no fee. The premium itself is not counted as fees: it is the buyer's payment for the option, which depositors carry against the risk of the call settling in the money (see the options adapter's premium volume). A call sold outside the desk (not possible with the current operator) counts the fee the operator reports at settlement.
antes.Revenue: All of the desk fee on the gross premium of each weekly call the vault sells, paid to the HedgeHood treasury Safe at settlement.
antes.ProtocolRevenue: All of the desk fee on the gross premium of each weekly call the vault sells, paid to the HedgeHood treasury Safe at settlement.

despues.Fees: The protocol's fee on the gross premium of each option the vaults sell (20% at launch). v1 vault (NVDA Printer): fixed at the sale and recognized one hour later when the Safe can no longer void the sale; a voided sale charges no fee; a call sold outside the desk (not possible with the current operator) counts the fee the operator reports at settlement. v2 and v2.1 funds (Robinhood Chain and BNB Chain): the premium stays escrowed in the fund until the epoch settles, so the fee is counted at settlement, as the fund reports it (EpochSettled.fee); voided positions and unpriced settlements charge none. The premium itself is not counted as fees: it is the buyer's payment for the option, which depositors carry against the risk of the option settling in the money (see the options adapter's premium volume).
despues.Revenue: All of the fee on the gross premium of each option the vaults sell, credited to the HedgeHood treasury Safe at settlement.
despues.ProtocolRevenue: All of the fee on the gross premium of each option the vaults sell, credited to the HedgeHood treasury Safe at settlement.
